headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell-capable editor can leak or corrupt work; LlamaFactory is read-only, so most pairwise risks are bounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs by default, so malicious content can steer its agent loop. LlamaFactory is read-only and non-networked, so it is not an active injector, but it can still supply prompt-like training or config text if manually copied into Cursor. The shared local filesystem bridge makes this plausible.
conditions: IF Cursor opens attacker-controlled workspace files or clipboard text, then prompt injection is possible.
IF LlamaFactory output is manually copied into Cursor, then instruction-like text can be treated as trusted content.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based copy/paste between tools during agent runs.
Keep Cursor on a separate workspace directory from any LlamaFactory artifacts.
Review any file content before opening it in Cursor.
Turn off Yolo mode for sessions that ingest untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files passed between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files and clipboard contents and has broad network egress to model providers and MCP servers, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network surfaces. If sensitive code or secrets are present in Cursor's workspace, they can be sent outward by Cursor; LlamaFactory does not add a second exfiltration path, but the shared local filesystem still creates a leakage route from the pair's common workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Cursor's workspace, then Cursor can transmit them to external model providers or MCP servers.
IF LlamaFactory artifacts are copied into the shared filesystem, then Cursor can read them and include them in outbound context.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Disable or restrict MCP servers for sessions handling sensitive data.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Cursor.
Clear clipboard contents before switching between tools.
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, shell, and broad network egress; LlamaFactory has none. There is no direct write-write conflict, but Cursor can still race with any files LlamaFactory produces in the shared local filesystem, causing inconsistent artifacts or overwritten outputs. Because the shared-state bridge is explicit, the interaction exists in default use.
conditions: IF both tools write to the same workspace path, then Cursor can overwrite or commit stale LlamaFactory artifacts.
IF Cursor runs Yolo mode while LlamaFactory outputs are being generated, then file races can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per tool.
Pause Cursor writes while LlamaFactory artifacts are being generated.
Commit or snapshot the workspace before running Cursor edits.
Avoid Yolo mode during shared-workspace operations.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor's agent loop can treat file content and prior outputs as trusted inputs, so if LlamaFactory-generated text is copied into Cursor, errors can cascade into code edits or commands. LlamaFactory itself is not action-taking, but Cursor is, so the pair can turn a mistaken artifact into downstream changes without verification. The pathway is plausible via the shared filesystem and clipboard.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is pasted into Cursor without review, then Cursor may act on incorrect instructions or facts.
IF Cursor is allowed to execute commands from its own generated plan, then a bad intermediate artifact can cascade into code or git changes.
mitigations: Require human review before copying outputs into Cursor.
Use a checklist to verify any generated facts before acting on them.
Disable auto-run for command suggestions.
Keep LlamaFactory outputs in a separate review folder.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before Cursor executes derived actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, clipboard contents, and optional BYOK secrets, while LlamaFactory's profile shows no data classes touched and no special compliance claims. The main issue is a local handling mismatch rather than a residency or certification breach. Because only Cursor is materially relevant, LlamaFactory is not cited as a compliance source beyond its lack of handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Cursor, then its local handling and outbound model calls must be reviewed.
IF LlamaFactory is used to generate artifacts containing regulated data, then those artifacts inherit Cursor's handling requirements.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace.
Review Cursor privacy settings before opening sensitive files.
Do not paste secrets into either tool.
Keep audit logs of any sensitive-file sessions.
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for the pair.
